title: Targeting Neuronal Fiber Tracts for Deep Brain Stimulation Therapy Using Interactive, Patient-Specific Models
protocol: Download and install FreeSurfer.
Create a patient directory using recon-all -s patientName -i /Full/Path/To/nii.
Run FreeSurfer's automated segmentation with recon-all -s patientName -all.
Convert "aseg.auto.mgz" out of FreeSurfer's proprietary .mgz format using mri_convert.
Download and install Slicer.
Use DWIConverter module in Slicer to reconstruct the 41 separate acquisitions into a single volume.
Specify the Input Dicom Data Directory where the DWI data is located.
Select the DicomToNrrd radio button and provide the name of the output DWI volume.
Create a Tensor mask with the Diffusion Weighted Volume Masking module.
Leave the threshold parameter at the default of 0.5.
Convert a single DWI volume to a Diffusion Tensor (DTI) volume using the DWI to DTI Estimation method.
Use the mask created in the previous step as the Diffusion Tensor Mask.
Set the estimation parameters to Least Squares.
Check the Shift Negative Eigenvalues option.
Save the newly created DTI volume in NRRD format.
Create a surface mesh of an encapsulation layer 0.5 mm thick surrounding the entire lead.
Load the brain surface created in Part 1 to serve as the outer boundary of the FEM.
Create two concentric box surfaces surrounding the DBS lead to control the mesh density around the electrode.
Create a point cloud with a single point located in each distinct region of the mesh.
Use the "InterfaceWithTetGen" module to create the whole brain mesh.
Use two cascading CreateGeometricTransform modules to rotate the electrode in the X plane.
Set first module to 1.00 on Axis Y for rotation.
Set second module to 1.00 on Axis X for rotation.
Connect a TransformMeshWithTransform module for every transform and object that needs transformation.
Create a GenerateSinglePointProbeFromField module and connect its geometry port to the ViewScene module.
Move the sphere around in the ViewScene window by holding shift and left-clicking.
The point probe module updates the sphere's location upon release.
Use a TransformMeshWithTransform module to translate each part of the electrode geometry with the point probe location.
Apply the two rotation transforms and the translation from the point probe widget to every object except the brain surface.
Load the DTI volume created in Step 1.
Set the data onto the tetrahedral mesh output from InterfaceWithTetGen using MapFieldDataFromSourceToDestination with the linear('weighted') option.
Set the shaft region conductivity to 1e-6 and the contact region to 1e6 using CalculateFieldData.
Pipe the field into BuildFEMatrix.
Pipe the brain surface used in the meshing process from Step 2 into SetFieldDataToConstantValue.
Set the value to 0 to create a voltage sink on the entire brain surface.
Use InsertVoltageSource to place the voltage values on the tetrahedral mesh output from InterfaceWithTetGen.
Calculate the FieldCenter value from the ReportFieldInfo module on one of the contact surfaces for monopolar stimulation.
Set the field data on this point to -1 Volts.
Use InsertVoltageSource to place the point source in the tetrahedral mesh inside a contact location.
Join the output of the two InsertVoltageSource modules.
Pipe the output into ApplyFEMVoltageSource along with the output of BuildFEMatrix.
Pipe the two outputs of ApplyFEMVoltageSource into SolveLinearSystem.
Select the Conjugate Gradient solving method and Jacobi as the preconditioner.
Use SetFieldData to place the voltage solution matrix onto the tetrahedral mesh for a 3D representation of voltage distribution.
Pipe the result of SetFieldData into ExtractSimpleIsosurface.
Open the UI to the Quantity tab and set the number of evenly-spaced isovalues to 10.
Connect the output of ExtractSimpleIsosurface to a ShowField module.
Connect the ShowField module to the ViewScene module to display the Isosurfaces as transparent with a rainbow color map scaled to the min and max of the voltage solution.
